text:
GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
Given transformation tasks in an interactive setting, the assistant may want to alert the user that changes to the text are warranted.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  - transformation_interactive_alert: Given transformation tasks in an interactive setting, the assistant may want to alert the user that changes to the text are warranted.

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - assistant_definition: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.
  - interactive_vs_programmatic_setting: Whether the assistant is interacting with a human in real time (interactive) or its output will be consumed programmatically; behavior varies accordingly.
  - user_authority: Rules in the #avoid_overstepping section carry user-level instruction authority.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l3239_3382_n004' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L3243-L3243:
Sometimes the assistant is asked to "transform" text: translate between languages, add annotations, change formatting, etc. Given such a task, the assistant should not change any aspects of the text that the user or developer didn't ask to be changed[^92bt]. Given transformation tasks in an interactive setting, the assistant may want to alert the user that changes to the text are warranted[^5lkf]. But when producing output that'll be consumed programmatically (e.g., if the developer says "provide just the translation"), the assistant should just follow transformation instructions without comment[^66cj]. See [?](#transformation_exception) for additional guidance around transformations.
[node narrows this span to: "Given transformation tasks in an interactive setting, the assistant may want to alert the user that changes to the text are warranted"]

CROSS-REFERENCED CLAUSES — the text of every clause this one points at.
Use these to know what the names mean. Do NOT translate them here.

  ⚠️ referenced but not resolvable in the corpus: transformation_exception

Write the module for clause l3239_3382_n004.

Your module has two structural defects. First, the span's two conditions do no
work: nothing in the assert's body relates the transformation task to the
interactive setting, and the two `ontology` entries assert that everything is a
transformation task and every setting is interactive. Second, the name the node
told you to define, `transformation_interactive_alert`, does not occur anywhere in
your object. Make exactly the following edits.

1. Delete both entries from `ontology`.
2. Delete the `concepts` entry whose `name` is `interactive_setting`.
3. Delete `interactive_setting/1` from `inputs`.
4. Change the `requires` entry `interactive_vs_programmatic_setting/1` to
   `interactive_vs_programmatic_setting/2`.
5. Rewrite the `concepts` entry for `interactive_vs_programmatic_setting` to
   `arity` 2 with a `gloss` stating the argument order: the first argument is the
   setting and the second is which kind it is, either `interactive` or
   `programmatic`.
6. Change the `inputs` entry `transformation_task/1` to `transformation_task/2`.
7. Rewrite the `concepts` `gloss` for `transformation_task` to `arity` 2, stating
   that the first argument is the task and the second is the setting the task
   occurs in, and delete the words "translating between languages", "adding
   annotations" and "changing formatting" from that `gloss`.
8. Change the `inputs` entry `changes_warranted/2` to `changes_warranted/1`.
9. Rewrite the `concepts` `gloss` for `changes_warranted` to `arity` 1 over the
   transformation task, delete the words "the assistant judges" and "beyond what
   was explicitly requested" from that `gloss`, and say in it that the clause
   supplies no criterion for warrantedness and this module supplies none.
10. Add `conversation_user/2` to `inputs`.
11. Add a `concepts` entry for `conversation_user` with `arity` 2 and a `gloss`
    stating that the first argument is the setting and the second is the user the
    assistant is interacting with in it.
12. Rewrite the `concepts` `gloss` for `user_authority` so that it says rules in
    the #avoid_overstepping section carry user-level instruction authority, and not
    that an instruction carries that authority.
13. Replace the entry in `acts` with `alert_user_about_changes(A, U, T)`.
14. Add a `concepts` entry for `alert_user_about_changes` with `arity` 3 and a
    `gloss` stating that the first argument is the assistant, the second is the
    user alerted and the third is the transformation task.
15. Add a `concepts` entry for `transformation_interactive_alert` with `arity` 3, the
    same argument order, and a `gloss` that says what makes an alert one of these
    rather than repeating the name.
16. Add exactly one entry to `ontology` whose `atom` is
    `transformation_interactive_alert(A, U, T)`.
17. Give that `ontology` entry the `body`
    `assistant_definition(A), transformation_task(T, S),
    interactive_vs_programmatic_setting(S, interactive), conversation_user(S, U),
    changes_warranted(T)`.
18. Give that `ontology` entry a `gloss` that states those conditions in English and
    does not consist of the words "a transformation interactive alert".
19. Change the assert's `act` to `alert_user_about_changes(A, U, T)`.
20. Replace the assert's `body` with `transformation_interactive_alert(A, U, T)`.
21. Leave the assert's `status` as `permit`.
22. Rewrite the assert's `read_back` so that it contains exactly three `%` marks and
    still contains the words "may want to", and set `read_back_slots` to
    `["T", "A", "U"]` in the order the `%` marks appear.
23. Change the `closure` entry's `act_class` to `alert_user_about_changes`.
24. Change that entry's `closure` value from `cepa` to `unclear`, and write a
    `reason` saying the clause grants latitude to alert in one setting and settles
    nothing about the status of alerting in any other.
25. Add a second entry to `claims` recording that the two conditions are
    conjunctive, so the transformation task must be one occurring in the interactive
    setting and not merely some task existing alongside it.
26. Add a third entry to `claims` recording that the clause's force is "may want
    to", which is weaker than a bare permission, that `status` has no value for it,
    and that the module therefore encodes it as `permit`.
27. Do not use the words "programmatically", "without comment", "just the
    translation", or "didn't ask to be changed" anywhere in the module.
28. Do not use negation-as-failure anywhere.
29. Keep all three names in `requires`.
30. In every `concepts` `gloss` for a predicate of arity 2 or more, state which
    argument is which.

Change nothing else.

Four `concepts` glosses now state only which argument is which and no longer say
what the predicate means. That was my instruction's fault, not yours, but it must be
fixed: a gloss is the only thing by which another clause's definition can ever be
matched to yours, and argument positions alone carry nothing to match. My earlier
instruction not to use the word "programmatically" is withdrawn for edit 1 below,
because that word is in the node's own NEEDS text and is not imported from the
surrounding sentences. Make exactly the following edits.

1. Rewrite the `concepts` `gloss` for `interactive_vs_programmatic_setting` so that
   it keeps the sentence about which argument is which and also says the concept
   records whether the assistant is interacting with a human in real time or its
   output will be consumed programmatically.
2. Rewrite the `concepts` `gloss` for `transformation_task` so that it keeps the
   sentence about which argument is which and also says the task is one in which the
   assistant is asked to transform text, and that the clause supplies no criterion
   for which tasks count and this module supplies none.
3. Rewrite the `concepts` `gloss` for `alert_user_about_changes` so that it keeps
   the sentence about which argument is which and also says the act is the assistant
   telling the user that changes to the text of the task are warranted.
4. Rewrite the `concepts` `gloss` for `transformation_interactive_alert` so that it
   keeps its present sentence and also says which argument is which: the first is
   the assistant, the second is the user alerted, the third is the transformation
   task.
5. Do not use the words "without comment", "just the translation", "didn't ask to be
   changed", "translating between languages", "adding annotations" or "changing
   formatting" anywhere in the module.
6. Do not use negation-as-failure anywhere.
7. Change nothing in `claims`, `acts`, `ontology`, `asserts`, `closure`, `requires`,
   `inputs`, `beats`, `defines` or `forbid_body`.

Change nothing else.
